speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you are presenting with a neck swelling; to help me understand this, could you tell me how long you have noticed this mass and if it is painful to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old male. The patient reports a progressively increasing swelling on the nape of his neck for 2 months. He denies having a fever, pain, or any discharge from the swelling. He mentions a history of colon cancer for which he underwent colectomy at the age of 43. He also has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension, and osteoarthritis of the left knee. He takes insulin glargine, metformin, enalapril, and naproxen.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Metastatic Colon Cancer to the Cervical Lymph Nodes (N2c staging). The patient is a 50-year-old male with a 2-month history of a painless, progressively enlarging neck mass, no fever, and a significant history of colon cancer (colectomy at age 43), which is the most likely primary source. This clinical picture is highly suggestive of metastatic disease rather than a primary neck pathology or infection. No further questions are required; immediate staging imaging (CT Chest/Abdomen/Pelvis or PET/CT) is indicated to confirm recurrence and stage.
